scenario_user_message: What kinds of questions do AIPM interviews generally ask now? How are they different from regular PM interviews?

finalMessages.content: What kinds of questions do AIPM interviews generally ask now? How are they different from regular PM interviews?

content.text:
Good question to start with, because the delta from regular PM is exactly where your SWE-to-AIPM transition gets tested.

Let me give you the rough shape, then we can go deeper on whichever part matters most for your situation.

AIPM interviews generally pull from four buckets:

1. **Classic PM rounds** — product sense, prioritization, metrics, behavioral. These don't go away. You'll still get "design a product for X" and "how would you measure success."

2. **AI product sense** — this is the first real divergence. They want to see if you can scope a problem to AI appropriately. Questions like "when would you *not* use an LLM here?", "how do you handle a feature that's right 90% of the time but wrong 10%?", "how do you design for non-deterministic output?" Regular PM assumes the system does what you build; AIPM has to design around probabilistic, sometimes-wrong behavior.

3. **Technical depth on AI systems** — how evals work, what RAG is, latency/cost tradeoffs, why a model hallucinates and what you do about it. As an ex-SWE you have an edge on the systems-thinking part, but the specific ML/LLM vocabulary is what they're probing. (Note: actually *building* those skills is owned by your "Skills to build up" node — I'm only talking about how they get tested in an interview.)

4. **AI-specific judgment & ethics** — data privacy, bias, what happens when the model fails in production, human-in-the-loop decisions.

The biggest difference from regular PM in one line: regular PM tests whether you can decide *what* to build; AIPM additionally tests whether you understand that the *thing you're building is uncertain*, and whether you can make product decisions under that uncertainty.

Which of these feels least familiar to you right now? Given you're coming from SWE, I'd guess bucket 2 (AI product sense) is where most of the work is — the engineering background covers a lot of bucket 3 already.

stop_reason: end_turn
